reviews.title: Horde covering team members
reviews.text: I can’t click on any of my teammates when the hoard is in the same spot as us and it’s really frustrating.

reviews.title: Terrible App
reviews.text: A terrible app that will constantly remind you that you have not allowed it to send you annoying notifications. Only used it because our company uses it.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: Fun

reviews.title: This game sucks
reviews.text: I was looking for a free walking app that plays like a game but every time I turn around, they’re trying to charge me. I was finally able to get the joint code but now they want to charge me for a game ticket as well. I can only imagine that once I pay for the game ticket they’re gonna find something else to charge me for. This is not a free app like they advertised. It’s an absolute lie.

reviews.title: App needs work
reviews.text: My company used this app for a team challenge and has used it in the past. This time was very frustrating, there were so many issues with syncing and almost a full day when the app wouldn’t even load.

reviews.title: Load Time still a challenge
reviews.text: I like the overall function of this app and different themes available for team challenges.  Every time I need to sync steps I have to wait through an extremely long load screen animation.  Cool logo, I’m tired of seeing it change texture. Just let me sync steps and slay goblins/zombies/aliens.

reviews.title: Awful Customer Support
reviews.text: The app stopped tracking my steps for our challenge and when I messaged support they took 2 full days to respond and responded with a very unhelpful response and no regard to help resolve the issue. I’d think twice about choosing to use this app for your step challenge because if anything goes wrong you will not get any help.

reviews.title: Work Challenge App
reviews.text: The app shuts down a lot and continued to log us out during a work challenge.  Also the app doesn’t always sync with Health right away so it’s sometimes hard to tell how many steps you’ve truly accrued.  It definitely still needs some work, but overall we enjoyed it.

reviews.title: Great motivation
reviews.text: This helped me to want to get my steps in more and motivate myself to push

reviews.title: Not clear on objectives
reviews.text: Didn’t understand this game most of time.   Actions and rules were inconsistent.   For example if you averaged 15000 steps it only counted 2000

reviews.title: How do you even play this?
reviews.text:
Downloaded the app expecting it to be playable. Turns out you need some sort of code to even play. It’s unclear how the code is even obtained. All this should be stated upfront and clearly. My best guess is that companies or organizers go through some sort of process online (outside the app) to create a code (which costs a lot of money) which can then be played by others. Once again, very unclear. Is this game not actually meant to be played by those who find it on the App Store but rather through organizations/companies who are doing team building or clubs creating an exercise regiment ?

There should be a free version that doesn’t require going outside the app to play.

reviews.title: Fix the glitches
reviews.text: Watch out because some of the games glitch and it screws up the whole competition. I’ve got thousands of steps banked and it won’t let me cash in or play. I’m just stuck at an obstacle which keeps hurting me. Need to fix the glitches.

reviews.title: App needs work
reviews.text: I do a challenge every year with my work team. I enjoy a lot of elements to the challenge. I will say having it surge up to 12k steps needed on the last week when we start at a goal of 5k week one is too extreme. We are working professionals! Also I do feel the zombies should lighten up a little during the workday. Again, working professionals doing this app mostly I imagine. Lastly, why does the app and typing in the group chat have to be sideways? This was my team’s number one complaint. As well, long term, would love to see more action take place for my character than just beating the zombies with a broom. But mostly, I love it! Just think some app features could be better in design and functionality

reviews.title: Not very well thought out!
reviews.text:
Unless you’re putting in 1000 steps by breakfast and another 1000 Steps every couple hours the Horde catches you!  Even though you could put in 4000-5000 Steps when you get of work!! 

This doesn’t make any Sense for people that have Desk jobs or are tied up in meetings!

reviews.title: Motivational!
reviews.text: I needed something to help me get moving. I was like zombies! I did a searched on the interwebs and found a review about this app. It seemed like it was right up my alley. I have been getting my 5k steps in and then some. And I started jogging. This app is fun and easy to use. And the challenges fit my budget. I look forward to completing my first challenge.

reviews.title: Power points need to be adjusted
reviews.text: I enjoyed the camaraderie of the team event that I participated in.  I have to use my phone to count my steps since I don’t use a Fitbit or any other device.  So, getting power points was extremely low just doing the steps per day.  I think that should be adjusted so that when you reach your goal each day, that there is a bonus of power points.  Outside activities should add points but they should be of less consequence, since the “game” is about getting your daily “steps” in and helping your team get to the safe house.

reviews.title: Sync issues with Garmin Venu 3
reviews.text: I had tonnes of sync issues, most days it was 10+ hours behind unfortunately so my team didn’t get the benefit of the steps.

reviews.title: Loved the game
reviews.text: We did a 4 week challenge and it was difficult getting others to participate, but we came in 7th out of 9 teams. I’m just glad we weren’t last.

reviews.title: Mediocre
reviews.text: Game is okay, but I found it immensely frustrating that there was a cap on inputting steps. Also it’s beyond stupid that you can’t convert steps into power for healing or fighting obstacles. It makes the game purposeless and irritating rather than fun. I’m not likely to play this game again because of how dumb the rules were.

reviews.title: Glad it was free
reviews.text: In addition to all the reports about it being “slow”, the gameplay is demoralizing from day 1. The “horde” is upon you and taking health before you have even had a chance to meet your first day step goal.  And the “team step” dynamic inherently favors small teams with the minimum number of participants.

reviews.title: Thought I was joining a walking challenge.
reviews.text:
I thought I was joining a walking challenge.  To see how many steps me and my team could get together and racing other teams to the end and to avoid zombie things… 

That wasn’t it. 
Week one- we started out walking.  Some of my teammates weren’t walking - we needed to remind them that they joined the challenge and start walking.   

We came across our first obstacle of K.A.R.E.bots.  This stopped us from uploading steps. We needed PowerPoints to beat the bots.  Well week one we don’t need a lot of power points so we could easily beat the bots and move forward. 

Well each week, we needed more steps- no problem, it’s a walking challenge, makes sense.  Well each week the value of power points needed to kill the K.A.R.E.bots also increases.  I don’t think any of us figured out how to get more PowerPoints, but we definitely got annoyed and frustrated because we couldn’t add the steps we earned because we were stuck at the K.A.R.E.bots and couldn’t move until they were defeated.  So we would end up stuck in the middle of the course getting best up.  You also use the PowerPoints to heal yourself if you get best up, so in order to survive you heal yourself before killing bots and your just stuck.  So you have 1000s of atps that don’t get tracked as your just stuck.  And if your teammates don’t do their part there’s nothing you can do. 

Due to the stupid cycle of K.A.R.E.bots and needing to defeat them before being able to log steps AND the Increae in the instances of K.A.R.E.bots in the path for each week do the challenge, had my group not even finish the course after the first week. 

Instead of tracking my steps, I ended up just trying g to try to earn PowerPoints to survive the obstacles to say I finished the challenge.  

It took ALL OF THE FUN out of the challenge.  Instead of encouraging each other to keep walking track those step, it turned into… to hate this app, stupid bots, I’m giving up.   Half of our team dropped out because the fun of the challenge was lost to the K.A.R.E.bots.  

I’m very disappointed.  I never thought my team would win, but some of use spent the first two weeks walking together, which was the coal of joining.  By the third week we were just frustrated to be bothered.  We are stuck at bots and would be able to track the steps anyhow.  

I do NOT recommend this app unless you are someone who already walks/runs  a lot already and you want to show off how much you exercise and be rewarded for your hard work.

reviews.title: Just Ok
reviews.text: I used this app for a school wide contest. It was not fun, and the teams weren't even with the amount of people making it impossible to win. Also, there were many times it didn't count my steps. The way it is laid out is also very confusing.

reviews.title: Fun
reviews.text: This game is very fun and keeps you engaged. I had a blast playing it with my coworkers.

reviews.title: Frustrating
reviews.text: Difficult to fight bots and be held back and unable to sync steps. Finishing five weeks only to be held back in the 6th week was also disappointing. We worked very hard and we didn’t finish.

reviews.title: Fun with friends but the app is inconsistent.
reviews.text: We enjoy the competition with our group, but our steps count on our fitbits, etc, NEVER matched what the game would pick up. The help feature is not helpful at all.

reviews.title: Great app
reviews.text: I enjoyed this app challenge as it helped me get back active. I’m feeling better fit and even lost a frw pounds.

reviews.title: Slow
reviews.text: So unbelievably slow to open this app. You’ll get a notification that the horde is upon you, and by the time you open the app someone has already defeated the horde. Takes an entire minute to simply open it. Graphics are cool but it’s hardly engaging. The only interactive part of it is defeating the hordes, and unless you’re the person on the team with the app already open and loaded you’ll never get to interact with the game apart from uploading your steps.

reviews.title: Bugs
reviews.text: Please fix app steps some times to add up and also its takes way to much to get just one power punch to fight robots could b a good fun app but steps don’t always generate and take way too much to get one power punch and cost tooo many power punches to fight just one robot

reviews.title: Uploading issue
reviews.text: Each time I open the app I have to read through all the little instructional statements.  Is there a way to stop that?  It say “loading complete” but still slowly displays the information.

reviews.title: It is hard to get it work
reviews.text: This is the kind of app that you have to reinstall several times, read the help, go through hoops, and it still doesn't work.

reviews.title: Beware $$$
reviews.text: Very disappointed. Once you create your character, there is no way to start a mission for free, and you can only join one if you’re given a code from someone.  There’s no in-app purchasing for the mission either, it redirects to an external website.  Not for individuals looking for a fitness challenge, look elsewhere.

reviews.title: Fun game but long load times
reviews.text: Fun team building game and if you’re competitive it helps encourage steps and activity. My only gripe is that it takes FOREVER to load the game; say you get a notification that there’s an obstacle, you open the app and it takes literally two minutes to finish loading. By the time you open the app and get to the game the obstacle has been cleared. It’s only if you actively have the app open and exercise, you’ll move forward enough to make it to an obstacle and be able to defeat it. I don’t even close out my app, it’s there running in the background but the load time still takes years

reviews.title: Lots of fun!
reviews.text: The only thing missing is if you are out the safe house for days, there is nothing to do except wait for the next week and just get your daily step goal. Maybe the zombies can try to break in and you need to use power points to keep them out?

reviews.title: Cheaters
reviews.text: It’s cool until you compete against a team with 1-2 people achieving 80k+ steps a day for 2 days and they’re finished. This app will never get my money again. Such a waste.

reviews.title: Dysfunctional App (Stay Away!)
reviews.text: There are two categories of people using this app:  1) clueless enthusiasts who don’t mind rebooting their phone every other time they try to use the app, and 2) those held hostage by an incompetent HR department who picked this app as a prerequisite to earning health care benefits.

reviews.title: Needs Balancing
reviews.text: The game is really fun but really poorly balanced. The ideal way to win is to only recruit five people getting 10k steps a day. If you actually open up the team to all employees you wind up penalized for any underachievers. Instead of everyone feeling valued or like their effort matters, the higher achievers have to do extra work to balance out everyone else, instead of the teams working together it becomes very clear early on if victory is even achievable.

reviews.title: Moved More but frustrated by the game itself
reviews.text: I think this was a great motivation to get moving but the actual app and game left much to be desired. It was not a good fit for our team.

reviews.title: Doesn’t work well across time zones
reviews.text:
It is fun, but teams on the east coast always reach the Safehouse first thus earning points that teams in other (especially west) can never earn.  Is there a way to make it more fair?  Even our division is spread across time zones, and that is a bit frustrating.  
Another problem is that the app just won’t open sometime.  I just get a pulsing red hand.

reviews.title: Fun but has a very disappointing aspect.
reviews.text:
My husband got invited to join a work participation race. Everybody was excited and since he was doing it I joined in on the Freeplay quests.

 Before the game started he was excited enough that he was looking at the pay platforms wanting to see if we could start family challenges after the work challenge ended. 

After a week of us walking 5 miles a day He experienced a huge flaw in this game. His entire team hasn’t participated including the managers who were boasting excitement prior to the start. 
He went from almost no daily steps to walking 5 miles a day to participate. His efforts are split between 7 people who haven’t logged even 2 steps and his efforts alone are greater than the participants on the winning team. 

Why is it not mandatory that if after 3 days of non participation the dead weight gets dropped and the actual participants get regrouped and shuffled to participating teams? 

He’s carried the entire 7 person team and they’ve come in and used his exercise points to heal themselves but not contributed anything. Because of their lack of effort he’s not going to experience the safe house, and yet he’s put in 3 times the effort of anyone on the team ranked in 1st place. But because he couldn’t walk the extra 26 miles in 2 days to carry the team to the finish is kind of messed up. There should be a safeguard to combat those who consistently ride the game on others efforts. 

Those non contributing people have obviously been doing this a while because they have special in-game reward based extras. 

The idea of this game is awesome and could be a good motivation tool. However, the lack of options if you get put into a team that doesn’t participate is very discouraging and really makes you want to say “forget this, and why bother?”.

reviews.title: Tracks steps. Not much else
reviews.text: I didn’t really get the plot or the point. You just upload your steps every day. Hard to see how you compare to others. A 17,000 step day seems about the same as a 5,000 step day. As a work event, I’d say opposite of team building.

reviews.title: Great motivational game to get in shape thriving off of your peers
reviews.text: This game has kept me competitive if I notice I was short on my steps before bedtime I would go for a night walk just to make it up started wearing my phone during soccer basketball or any of my activities to get my steps in everything counts great game.

reviews.title: Fantastic but a big problem!
reviews.text:
This is a super fun super great super amazing idea and I was having a blast competing in it…at first

Turns out there is one big problem. At the start of a challenge you pick teams and I didn’t know by picking a team with ten people in it you must walk ten steps to move the team forward one step. While a team of one person only has to walk one step to move the team forward a step.

My work did this walking challenge with a bunch of office workers that don’t walk much at all. So half my team isn’t contributing. I’ve walked 60,000 steps in two days and my team isn’t halfway done with the first challenge. Meanwhile, one guy on a team by himself has walked 30,000 steps and finished the area getting the lead.

It kills the fun. Teams should be required or made into much smaller maximums and the making an extra step for every team member should be something we are warned about before being locked into teams

reviews.title: Overall having fun.
reviews.text: The concept is fun and motivating. The app itself needs more direction. I’ve read the overall directions several times but still haven’t figured out some things. My team has 10 players and I can only select the players in the forefront for their specs. No direction on how to see entire team. No direction on how to chat with team. It was trial and error to figure it out. I am. It a gamer so I it drives me nuts to have to learn as I go.

reviews.title: Good but needing more
reviews.text: This is my second time playing one of these challenges and it’s fun, but it needs more past the point of the Safehouse. People tend to put in a lot of effort for 2-3 days to make the Safehouse, but once they reach it their numbers tank for the rest of the week. There should be something that should motivate people throughout the week besides just the daily goal (which isn’t that difficult to get). Maybe have some extra side challenges inside the Safehouse people can compete for to gain extra victory points or something. That’s been my main constant gripe with this challenge.

reviews.title: Too easy to cheat
reviews.text: Allowing any manual input will attract cheating.

reviews.title: notifications????
reviews.text: what happened to push notifications??? they worked for a day and now my team and i are trying to message each other and don’t get any notifications. we don’t know when the zombies are ready to fight/attack. i even uninstalled and reinstalled the app.

reviews.title: This App Needs Serious Work
reviews.text:
I have played this twice now - a year ago and right now. The app has zero evolution or improvement. Many members have sync issues. Last year I was ok with my garmin watch, but this year I need to restart my app like every 2 hours if I need to sync. In the 2 weeks so far, the app crashed and restarted at least 10 times. The app has zero innovation- no new avatar abilities. For weapons you can only do a club - how boring. No new enemies or app graphics. They keep saying you can play as a zombie, but the app has no help info on how that is done. Supposedly you need to just stand there and wait a day for the horde to catch you, then one more to zombify you. Why - why not just give the user the option to start as zombie instead of wasting days. And we all generate power, but there is very little to spend it on. The team could take on like 40 times more zombies before we would be short on power.

The bare basics of the app somehow work. And I do enjoy stepping and the competition. We figured out that if you don’t balance out your teams, then the weak teams will just give up, as there is little chance of catching the lead team after a week.

We use week one to get stats on everyone, and then we build complete new teams before week 2. Teams are rebalanced so that each team has the same capacity to win. When the race is close, the competitive spirit grows and pushes us for more steps. This is when it gets fun.

I like the app basics and the whole idea. I just wish the app owners put in some innovation and improvements, and fix the syncs and app stability.

reviews.title: Don’t use this
reviews.text: I played this at my workplace but soon found out that it was only accurate with Apple Watches. I bought an iTouch fitness tracker just to play and people who didn’t even workout (with Apple Watches) were beating me in the game. I would even double my workouts and nothing changed. Needs work!

reviews.title: Please let us skip the tutorial
reviews.text:
I’m writing a 1 star review to get the dev’s attention

When I uninstall and reinstall the app please don’t make me go through the entire tutorial again! It’s such a pain to have to keep tapping next, wait for the next message to pop up, repeat 50 times until it’s all finally finished

It would be great if there’s just a “skip” button. Maybe you could only let people skip if it’s their 2nd+ race so that they have to take the tutorial on their 1st race. But I’m sure you know that I have done a dozen of these so you should let me skip them. Thank you

reviews.title: The out break
reviews.text: Great competitive game get our steps in and keep us motivated!
